identity.title: Equivalence of Context and Parameter Updates in Modern Transformer Blocks

problem.claim: Characterize how context effects in modern transformer blocks can be represented as implicit parameter updates.

gap.claim: Prior theory described this equivalence for vanilla transformers, while its applicability to diverse modern LLM architectures was not addressed in the supplied abstract.

contributions.claim: An analytical result for Gemma-style blocks mapping context effects to rank-1 MLP weight patches and an RMSNorm-scale patch.
A constructive proof and algorithm extending the mapping to multi-layer models.
A controllability-based framework using input controllability and output controllability to characterize when perfect implicit weight patches are possible.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their work by extending context–parameter equivalence from vanilla transformers to modern architectures and unifying it through controllability properties.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report proving that Gemma-style block context effects can be perfectly represented by rank-1 MLP patches plus an RMSNorm-scale patch.
The authors report a constructive proof and algorithm for multi-layer models.
The authors report that perfect implicit weight patching is possible for any MLP whose inner function is input-controllable and outer function is output-controllable.

narrative_sequence.summary: Context effects in vanilla transformers had been represented as token-dependent rank-1 MLP weight patches.
The work first analyzes a Gemma-style block and adds an RMSNorm-scale patch to the rank-1 MLP patches.
It next supplies a constructive proof and algorithm for multi-layer models.
It introduces input/output controllability and states applicability across gating, normalization, mixture-of-experts, and sequential/parallel blocks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract moves from a concrete Gemma-style construction to a multi-layer algorithm and then to controllability conditions intended to cover multiple architectures.

lessons.interpretation: A concrete derivation can motivate a reusable abstraction when the abstraction preserves explicit sufficient conditions.
lessons.application: Present one architecture-specific mapping first, then state the general structural conditions and identify which model variants satisfy them.
lessons.exception: This sequence may be unsuitable when the abstraction lacks clearly stated conditions or when architecture-specific details are themselves the main contribution.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the definitions of input/output controllability or the algorithmic procedure.
No quantitative experiments, baselines, computational costs, or independent verification of the claimed proofs are supplied.
The meaning and scope of “perfect” mapping across the listed architectures are not detailed.
